newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's postboxes lose their crowns.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's postboxes lose their crowns.

text.p: A couple of taps with a cold chisel and the metal crown, a symbol of British sovereignty, fell to the ground with a dull clunk.
Lam Chi-wah is one of the contractors responsible for removing the British insignia from Hong Kong's 800 postboxes before the colony reverts to China at midnight on June 30.
"It usually takes about two minutes a box," he said on Wednesday as he covered the bolt holes of box number 45 with masking tape and daubed the bald spot with red enamel paint.
The Royal Mail plans to paint its red post vans and boxes a viridian green -- similar in hue to China's -- and adopt a humming bird logo in place of the crown representing the British monarchy.
Hong Kong has embarked on a wholescale purge of British symbols, icons and insignia as the handover nears.
